Cite & share Copy BibTeX Copy citation Copy link arXiv ↗ @misc{chen2026oamap, title = {OA-MAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Multimodal Framework for Interpretable Knee Osteoarthritis Progression}, author = {Sixu Chen and Mingrui Yang and Qiang Guan and Xiaojuan Li}, year = {2026}, eprint = {2610.12134}, archivePrefix = {arXiv}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12134} } This week’s top papers Abstract Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) progression prediction can support patient monitoring, requiring the integration of multimodal data and multidomain expertise. Moreover, isolated risk estimates provide limited insight underlying a prediction. To automate the progression assessment workflow and reduce manual effort while providing interpretable findings and supporting evidence, we present OA-MAP, an autonomous multi-agent framework for evidence-grounded assessment of structural and pain progression in KOA. The system incorporates modality-specific agents including MRI, X-ray, and clinical agents, together with a coordinator agent. This framework can autonomously recruit specialist agents, select tools for prediction and analysis, and retrieve literature as external evidence based on user request and available patient information. An uncertainty-informed human-in-the-loop mechanism enables clinicians to review and correct intermediate findings, triggering recomputation of affected results. We evaluate the prediction models using 600 participants from the FNIH Osteoarthritis Biomarkers Consortium cohort. On the test set of 100 participants, the fusion models achieve AUROCs of 0.80 for structural progression and 0.68 for pain progression. A case study illustrates how OA-MAP combines risk estimates with intermediate findings, cross-modal conflicts, literature support, and uncertainty indicators to support interactive review. selected_records.title: OA-MAP: Evidence-Grounded Multi-Agent Multimodal Framework for Interpretable Knee Osteoarthritis Progression

article.body:
OA-MAP combines multimodal agents to assess knee osteoarthritis progression

OA-MAP uses MRI, X-ray and clinical agents coordinated by a central agent to assess structural and pain progression in knee osteoarthritis. It can select prediction and analysis tools and retrieve literature based on the request and available patient information. An uncertainty-informed human-in-the-loop mechanism lets clinicians correct intermediate findings and trigger recomputation.

The prediction models were evaluated on 600 participants from the FNIH Osteoarthritis Biomarkers Consortium cohort. On a 100-participant test set, fusion models achieved AUROCs of 0.80 for structural progression and 0.68 for pain progression. The paper also reports a case study of interactive review. The available evidence gives no baseline comparison or independent replication, and does not establish performance in clinical deployment.
